title: What a URL category entry may contain, and category limits

prose.text: These rules decide whether an entry is accepted at all, which matters most for automation: {{bulk-add-all-or-nothing}}

{{regex-patterns}} {{category-type-filter}} The `type` filter rests on SDK and MCP behavior, not the captured contract {{divergence:type-filter-parameter}}. Which field a TLD category takes its entries in is open {{gap:tld-category-entries}}.
{{category-quotas}} How entries match requests once accepted is in [[zia.url-categories.entry-matching]].

prose.label: Listing.
prose.text: The MCP source says the listing does not paginate and ignores page inputs {{mcp-list-unpaginated}}. Whether the keyword-counts parameter trims the response is disputed {{divergence:keyword-counts-parameter}}. {{mcp-lite-not-used}}

format-rules.statement: Entries must be lowercase, ASCII, in `host.domain` form, and must not include a scheme (`http://`).

quotes: Enter URLs in lowercase letters only.
The URL must not contain the protocol schema.
URLs should have the host.domain format
Only use ASCII characters.

underscore-rules.statement: Underscores are rejected in the TLD and in the second-level domain when a subdomain is present (`www.safe_march.com`), but allowed in subdomains, paths, and in the SLD of a URL with no subdomain (`safe_march.com`); a lone `_` cannot be a subdomain.

quotes: The URL must not contain an underscore ("_") in the top-level domain (TLD) or the second-level domain (SLD). However, it's allowed in the subdomain or the subdirectories of a URL
If a URL doesn't have a subdomain, then underscore ("_") is allowed in the SLD
The underscore ("_") alone cannot be a subdomain

no-tld-only.statement: A bare TLD such as `.gov` cannot be added as a URL entry.

quotes: You cannot add a URL that is only a TLD. For example, you cannot add ".gov" as a URL

length-limits.statement: A URL entry is at most 1,024 characters, its domain at most 255 characters before any colon, and each domain label at most 63 characters.

quotes: The URL length cannot exceed 1,024 characters.
The domain name before the colon (":") cannot exceed 255 characters
The domain name between periods (".") cannot exceed 63 characters

bulk-add-all-or-nothing.statement: Adding URLs to a custom category is all-or-nothing: one invalid URL rejects the whole request with an error, so automation must validate every entry first.

quotes: When adding URLs to a custom URL category, if a single URL uses an invalid format, the request is rejected and produces an error code.

non-english.statement: URL Filtering does not support non-English characters outside the ISO/IEC 8859-1 character set.

quotes: Non-English characters are not supported in URL Filtering, except those from the ISO/IEC 8859-1 character set.

keywords-whole-uri.statement: Custom keywords match anywhere in the whole URI, so a `gambling` keyword also matches a search URL such as `www.google.com/search?q=gambling`.

quotes: As custom keywords are applicable to the entire URI, if you went to www.google.com and searched for "gambling" the search results would also be blocked since the word gambling appears in the URI

category-quotas.statement: Default limits: 25K custom URLs or TLDs across all categories (more via a Custom URLs subscription), 64 custom categories (1,024 via Support), 256 keywords per category with 2,048 across all categories, 2,048 keywords retaining their parent category across all categories, and a combined 2,048 custom keywords plus retaining-parent keywords per organization.
category-quotas.conditions: Corrected on recapture (2026-10-18): previously "Default limits: 25K custom URLs or TLDs across all categories (more via a Custom URLs subscription), 64 custom categories (1,024 via Support), 256 keywords per category with 2,048 across all categories, and 2,048 keywords retaining their parent category per organization."

quotes: The default limit for custom URLs/TLDs is 25K.
Contact your Zscaler Account team to subscribe to up to an additional 50K custom URLs/TLDs.
The default limit for custom categories is 64.
Contact Zscaler Support to increase the limit to a maximum of 1,024 categories.
Custom Keywords per Category | 256 keywords | There can be a maximum of 2,048 custom keywords across all categories.
Keywords retaining parent category per Category | 2,048 keywords | There can be a maximum of 2,048 keywords retaining the parent category across all categories.
Total Custom Keywords and Keywords retaining parent category per Organization | 2,048 keywords

regex-patterns.statement: Custom categories can match by regex (`urlType: REGEX` with `regexPatterns`) instead of exact entries; patterns are 3 to 255 characters, at most 256 across all categories, and the feature must be enabled by Zscaler Support. The console walkthrough does not show this path, so odd-looking tenant entries may be patterns.

quotes: For regex, the patterns can be specified using the regexPatterns and regexPatternsRetainingParentCategory fields.
Note: To enable the Regex feature, contact Zscaler Support.
Multiple patterns can be added to a category. A pattern must be between 3 and 255 characters, and a maximum of 256 patterns can be added across all categories.

category-type-filter.statement: Custom categories have a `type` (`URL_CATEGORY` or `TLD_CATEGORY`). When listing, no type filter returns predefined plus custom `URL_CATEGORY` categories, and `ALL` returns predefined plus custom categories of every type.

quotes: // If categoryType is empty, no type filter is applied (returns predefined + custom URL_CATEGORY)
// If categoryType is "ALL", returns predefined + custom categories of all types

mcp-list-unpaginated.statement: The MCP URL-category list tool exposes `custom_only`, `type`, `search` and `contains_url`; its source says `/urlCategories` does not paginate and that page and page_size inputs had been silently ignored by the API. The captured Automate operation lists `customOnly` and `includeOnlyUrlKeywordCounts` as its only query parameters.

quotes: endpoint does not paginate and offers no way to omit a category's URL, keyword

``page`` /
    ``page_size`` were dropped on the floor by the API
"name": "customOnly",
"name": "includeOnlyUrlKeywordCounts",

mcp-lite-not-used.statement: The Python SDK has a `list_categories_lite` wrapper for the lightweight category list, and the MCP URL-category tool deliberately does not use it: its source says `/urlCategories/lite` takes no parameters, so it cannot filter, and it omits `configuredName`, the only handle a custom category has.

tld-category-entries.title: Which field holds TLD entries in a TLD_CATEGORY custom category
tld-category-entries.detail: The retired wildcard doc said to put TLD entries in `dbCategorizedUrls` on a `TLD_CATEGORY` category, but its citation only showed that the fields exist, and the Go SDK documents `dbCategorizedUrls` as the retain-parent URL list. Regular entries reject bare TLDs (claim no-tld-only); how TLD categories take their entries is unverified. Upstream terraform-provider-zia#497 (closed in v4.6.4) concerned importing this category type.

quotes: If set to true, the response only includes URL and keyword counts.

positions.says: Automate: the parameter, when true, makes the response include only URL and keyword counts for custom categories.

quotes: byte-for-byte equivalent, ``dbCategorizedUrls`` and ``ipRanges`` populated in

positions.says: MCP: a vendor-reported tenant capture with the parameter on and off was equivalent with the lists populated in both, so the tool does not send it.

keyword-counts-parameter.impact: Do not rely on the parameter to shrink the listing; the observation is one tenant capture, not proof that every tenant ignores it.

type-filter-parameter.summary: Whether the type query parameter exists

quotes: ``[query_params.type]`` {str}: Filter by category type.

positions.says: The Python SDK documents a `type` filter and the MCP tool sends it upstream.

quotes: query_params["type"] = args.type

positions.says: The MCP list tool sends `type` as an upstream query parameter.

quotes: "name": "includeOnlyUrlKeywordCounts",

positions.says: The captured Automate operation lists only customOnly and includeOnlyUrlKeywordCounts as query parameters.

type-filter-parameter.impact: The type filter rests on SDK and MCP behavior, not on the captured contract.
